threats.point: Profit is growing while operating cash flow is shrinking - an earnings-quality gap.
threats.evidence: Net profit 141 -> 182 Cr (TTM) but operating cash flow 227 Cr (Mar 2025) -> 190 Cr (Mar 2026)

threats.point: The stock has a history of very deep drawdowns.
A premium multiple versus peers can unwind quickly if growth slips.
Both foreign and domestic institutions have been reducing.
threats.evidence: FII -0.53 pp, DII -5.21 pp over the recent quarters

threats.point: Rolex Rings faced a near three-fold rise in ocean freight, higher fuel costs, and higher consumable costs following the escalation of the West Asia conflict.
threats.evidence: Risk disclosed in the filings: "We delivered this despite a near three-fold rise in ocean freight ,higher fuel cost and consumable costs following the escalation of the West Asia conflict." (concall ppt - 2026-11-01)

threats.point: Container availability at a reasonable cost remains a challenge for exports.
threats.evidence: Risk disclosed in the filings: "See, availability of containers at a proper cost is an issue." (concall transcript - 2026-08-01)

threats.point: A shortage of shop floor labor constrained output conversion despite a strong order book in Q1 FY27.
threats.evidence: Risk disclosed in the filings: "The constraint was labour availability, not demand. A shortage of workers on the shop floor meant we couldn't convert that order book into output at the pace we wanted." (concall ppt - 2026-08-01)

threats.point: Historically weak quarters (Mar, Sep, Dec) are still in the cycle.

swot.verdict: Strengths dominate the evidence (S31/W22/O28/T18), led by 'Capital efficiency is high - the business earns well above a normal cost of capital', with 68 points of weight still sitting on the weakness, opportunity and threat side.
